kind: Elementary algebra plus recorded operator audit
claim: Equal within-window token histograms imply identical mean pooled additive token-plus-position embeddings.
limit: The identity precedes GroupNorm and residual history; it does not force identical native quantizer codes.

claim: The hard level-5 code is constant on the examined clean data; replacing its prediction by code 11 while retaining the residual preserves recorded outputs.
limit: Constancy is empirical. It is not zero activation, universal uselessness, an optimization-history explanation or a measured speedup.

claim: Position-weighted pooling breaks the raw averaging symmetry and retains recorded reconstruction while diversifying level-5 codes.
limit: Known solutions are encoded. The frozen native generator does not call the repaired encoding operator, and no downstream robustness gain is established.

claim: Decoded values corrected at 9 can become wrong again; all early native full-grid cutoffs fail on the recorded hard test.
limit: This falsifies strict decoded-value locking, not every possible latent commitment. Early cutoff does not isolate level 9 or establish a phase transition.

claim: Oracle encoding of correct Sudoku solutions produces correction-then-degradation trajectories without generator execution.
limit: Sufficiency is not exclusive causal attribution. Similar rates are not an attributable fraction or a statistical equivalence result.

claim: LM1B and TinyStories audits do not reproduce a constant native level, although a raw additive pooling symmetry remains.
limit: Two tokenizers, finite text samples and different codebook capacities do not identify an architecture-wide defect or demonstrate every level useful.

claim: Raw final-token adoption followed by abandonment occurs in LM1B generation; true reconstruction corrections also revert in the oracle codec.
limit: The final generated token is a retrospective anchor, not ground truth. Raw and heuristic readouts are distinct. Invalid-loader trajectories are excluded, not results.

claim: The joint recovery-and-specificity criterion for omitting residual 9 is not met on the new 256-puzzle corpus.
limit: One omission, checkpoint and dose. No proof of globally blind adaptation, no equivalence claim and no exclusion of all forms of compensation.

claim: Frozen target-code substitutions write requested different digits in 784/1024 trials versus 0/1024 Gaussian controls on 128 new sources.
limit: Control matches local norm/support, not codebook geometry. No proof of new semantics, multi-cell compositionality or total context independence.

claim: Lookup supplies externally certified grids for 552/1024 new hard puzzles; checkpoint-specific secondary coverage is also recorded.
limit: The 30% coverage threshold followed favorable development results. Coverage does not establish novelty or an end-to-end performance gain.

claim: A sound validity-and-clue checker plus exact fallback cannot reduce exact success on unique-solution puzzles.
limit: A general verification argument, not a learned NCM mechanism. Multiple-solution reference fidelity and correctness of rejected fallback outputs are not guaranteed.

claim: Readout arithmetic means differ in the recorded session; the announced full-pipeline geometric interval includes one.
limit: One CPU session, 64 sources, all generator levels retained. No established end-to-end speedup or GPU/energy claim.

claim: The synthesis preserves eight campaign histories, dependencies, local protocols and their recorded verification scopes.
limit: Local freezes and same-agent software assertions are not external preregistration, independent review or proof against selection bias.

kind: Other recorded probe and intervention outcomes
claim: Initial confidence and conditional-revision probe results do not establish added hidden-state value or native metacognitive control.
limit: Probe families, fitting splits and observed baselines limit inference; these outcomes are retained rather than silently replaced by the four-pillar narrative.
